title: Kimberly Guilfoyle Resigns as U.S. Ambassador to Greece Amid Misconduct Allegations, NBC Reports
body:
Washington – The State Department announced Tuesday that Kimberly Guilfoyle, the U.S. ambassador to Greece, will step down immediately after the White House ordered her removal amid an internal misconduct investigation. The decision ends a brief, tumultuous tenure for the former Fox News commentator and high‑profile Trump campaign surrogate, whose appointment had been hailed by some as a reward for loyalty to the former president.

Guilfoyle, 56, was confirmed by the Senate in early 2024 and presented her credentials to Greek President Katerina Sakellaropoulou in March. Her diplomatic record, however, was quickly eclipsed by reports of a probe into alleged workplace harassment and abuse of authority within the embassy. While the State Department has not released specific details, officials indicated that the inquiry uncovered “credible allegations” that warranted immediate action. The White House, which had initially defended her appointment, reportedly concluded that her continued presence would be a distraction to U.S. interests in the region.

The resignation underscores the challenges the Biden administration faces in balancing political patronage with the demands of professional diplomacy. Guilfoyle’s nomination was part of a broader effort by the administration to fill a backlog of ambassadorships with individuals who had supported President Joe Biden’s 2020 campaign or, in this case, were closely tied to the previous administration’s political network. Critics have long warned that such appointments risk compromising the credibility of U.S. diplomatic missions, especially when appointees lack prior foreign‑service experience. In Guilfoyle’s case, her background in television and political consulting contrasted sharply with the complex geopolitical environment of the Eastern Mediterranean, where U.S. policy must navigate tensions between Greece, Turkey, and the energy disputes in the Aegean Sea.

Greek officials expressed disappointment at the abrupt departure but emphasized a desire for continuity in bilateral relations. In a brief statement, the Greek Ministry of Foreign Affairs said that “the United States remains a steadfast partner, and we look forward to working with the next ambassador to advance our shared interests in security, trade, and regional stability.” The embassy in Athens, which has been dealing with a surge in diplomatic activity related to NATO exercises and the ongoing Ukraine conflict, will now be led by a senior career diplomat on an interim basis while the State Department identifies a permanent replacement.

The episode also revives scrutiny of the broader pattern of misconduct allegations within U.S. diplomatic posts. Over the past two years, several embassies have been rocked by investigations into sexual harassment, intimidation, and retaliation, prompting calls for stricter oversight and a cultural shift within the Foreign Service. Congressional committees have urged the State Department to adopt more transparent reporting mechanisms and to ensure that political appointees receive the same standards of accountability as career officers. Guilfoyle’s case may become a catalyst for renewed legislative action aimed at tightening the vetting process for ambassadorial nominees.

Looking ahead, the Biden administration must quickly nominate a successor who can restore confidence both in Washington and in Athens. The ideal candidate will likely possess a blend of diplomatic experience and regional expertise, signaling a move away from purely political appointments toward a merit‑based approach. As U.S.-Greek cooperation deepens—particularly in defense procurement, energy diversification, and countering Russian influence—the next ambassador will inherit a portfolio that demands steady, seasoned leadership. The swift resolution of Guilfoyle’s resignation, while unsettling, offers an opportunity for the State Department to reaffirm its commitment to professional diplomacy and to rebuild trust with allies in a volatile part of the world.
